module_title: Formulas, Components, and the Macroeconomic Equation
introduction: At this level, we will break down the exact mathematical formulas and components that make up the Income and Expenditure methods. These formulas are the backbone of macroeconomics.

core_concepts.title: Components of the Income Method
core_concepts.description:
When you use the Income Method, you get 'NDP at Factor Cost' (NDP_FC). It has 3 main components: 1. Compensation of Employees (Wages, salaries, employer's contribution to PF). 2. Operating Surplus (Rent + Interest + Profit). 3. Mixed Income of Self-Employed. 
Formula: NDP_FC = COE + OS + MI.

core_concepts.title: Mixed Income (MI)
core_concepts.description: This is highly relevant for India. 'Mixed Income' is the income of the self-employed (like farmers, doctors, small shopkeepers) where it is impossible to separate how much of their income is a 'wage' for their labor and how much is 'profit' from their business.

core_concepts.title: Components of the Expenditure Method
core_concepts.description:
When you use the Expenditure Method, you get 'GDP at Market Price' (GDP_MP). It has 4 components: 
1. C = Private Final Consumption Expenditure (Households).
2. I = Gross Domestic Capital Formation (Investments by businesses).
3. G = Government Final Consumption Expenditure.
4. (X - M) = Net Exports (Exports minus Imports).
Formula: GDP_MP = C + I + G + (X - M).

core_concepts.title: Value Added Method (GVA)
core_concepts.description: Formula: Gross Value Added (GVA) = Value of Output - Intermediate Consumption. Summing up the GVA of all sectors (Primary, Secondary, Tertiary) gives the GDP of the nation.

important_entities.name: Operating Surplus
important_entities.significance: Examiners often ask what constitutes 'Operating Surplus'. Remember it is the income derived from property and entrepreneurship: Rent (from land), Interest (from capital), and Profit (from entrepreneurship).

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: In the Income Method, NEVER include 'Transfer Payments'. Transfer payments are one-way payments for which no productive service is rendered (e.g., Old-age pensions, scholarships, unemployment allowances, pocket money). They are excluded because they do not reflect actual current production.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Consumption + Investment + Government + Net eXports. This is the most famous macroeconomic equation in the world.

exam_strategy_tips: If a question asks 'Which component is the largest contributor to India's GDP from the expenditure side?', the answer is 'Private Final Consumption Expenditure (C)'. It makes up roughly 55-60% of India's GDP.
